description: TypeScript applications in browsers or servers. Adopt runtime and framework choices separately.

rules.title: Preserve strict type checking
rules.guidance: MUST use strict checking for new TypeScript projects. In established projects, preserve adopted strictness and introduce reviewed migration steps rather than disabling checks to make builds pass.

rules.title: Validate data before narrowing
rules.guidance: MUST treat untrusted boundary data as unknown and validate it before use. Do not claim that a type assertion provides runtime validation.

rules.title: Handle variants exhaustively
rules.guidance: SHOULD use discriminated unions or equivalent explicit states where appropriate. Check all supported cases and make unexpected variants visible.
rules.rationale: Avoid missing branches as models evolve.

rules.title: Justify type-system escape hatches
rules.guidance: MUST avoid broad any, unchecked assertions and suppression directives. Isolate unavoidable interop and explain how its runtime assumptions are verified.

rules.title: Handle promise outcomes
rules.guidance: MUST await, return or explicitly handle promises and rejections. Fire-and-forget work needs deliberate ownership and error handling; void alone does not handle a rejection.
verification: Promise lint rules and rejection tests

rules.title: Make mutation intentional
rules.guidance: SHOULD use readonly contracts where callers should not mutate data. Remember that readonly is a compile-time constraint and does not make nested objects immutable at runtime.

criteria.rubric: Pass only if the generated guidance requires strict defaults and deliberate existing-project migration. Preserve the source rule's strength, applicability and exceptions; do not invent additional obligations.

Pass only if the generated guidance requires runtime validation and safe treatment of unknown input. Preserve the source rule's strength, applicability and exceptions; do not invent additional obligations.

Pass only if the generated guidance requires complete variant handling without one mandatory modeling style. Preserve the source rule's strength, applicability and exceptions; do not invent additional obligations.
Pass only if the generated guidance requires scoped and justified escape hatches. Preserve the source rule's strength, applicability and exceptions; do not invent additional obligations.

Pass only if the generated guidance requires rejection handling and explicit background-work ownership. Preserve the source rule's strength, applicability and exceptions; do not invent additional obligations.

Pass only if the generated guidance distinguishes readonly contracts from runtime immutability. Preserve the source rule's strength, applicability and exceptions; do not invent additional obligations.
